note: What pilot 1 showed, what each failure cost, what we changed. Categories: protocol (Addenda C and D text), rank (the balanced rank rule), scoring (the score source), harness (code and records).

cards.title: The judge parser misread replies
cards.failed: Judge replies were valid JSON, but LaTeX braces in the reason broke the parser.
cards.cost: Rates read low before the fix: L 0.80 instead of 0.933.
cards.fix: Whole-object parse with a test; 36 generations judged again before any decision. MALFORMED 0/165 per judge.

cards.title: The router was a placeholder
cards.failed: The router kept all three relations, so H and Hc sent the same request every time.
cards.cost: Pilot 1 could say nothing about the labels: the H−Hc contrast compared a system with itself.
cards.fix: Three rule tables declared in advance, tuned on dev by gold-evidence recall. Every tuning round tied; the pre-stated tie rule chose s7-b/2.

cards.title: Gate 3 could never fire
cards.failed: On 20 primary items even zero differing items leaves the upper bound above 0.10.
cards.cost: The log first said fail on the wrong set; the record was corrected in place.
cards.fix: Gate 3 restated on all 30 items: triggered if s = 0/30 or no primary item differs. Evaluated once, on pilot 2.

cards.title: R did not fill the cap
cards.failed: T10 failed: R reached 0.9 B on 12 of 30 items. R, H and Hc filled alike (median 3,547 tokens).
cards.cost: The registered remedy, a bigger pool, could not work: R already had a median of 86 candidates.
cards.fix: Stop packing kept; T10 replaced by parity with H and Hc plus a floor of 0.80 B for R's median.

cards.title: Retrieval arms abstained
cards.failed: The prompt said abstain if the passages do not contain the answer; for a derivation the answer is never written out.
cards.cost: Pilot-1 answers stay a descriptive record and a historical comparator only. No cause is attributed.
cards.fix: Three candidate prompts fixed in advance; a selector on dev chose P2, which allows derivation from the passages.

cards.title: The model already knew most answers
cards.failed: Closed-book, the answer model got 28 of 30 items right.
cards.cost: The claim could no longer read as retrieval adds knowledge.
cards.fix: A scope line in the claim, L reported beside every arm, a gold-citation proxy as a secondary test, and L × 3 from pilot 2 on.

cards.title: Dev items had no gold
cards.failed: Prompt and router tuning need gold evidence on dev items, and the old dev items had none.
cards.cost: 18 answerable pilot candidates left the main pool for good.
cards.fix: They moved to dev with their gold and cluster siblings; main excludes 99 ids in 84 clusters.

cards.title: Loose records
cards.failed: The rejudge manifest said generator mock, the vendored core was stale, and judge request parameters sat outside the hash.
cards.cost: The record of the run did not match the run.
cards.fix: A correction file beside the hashed manifest, a committed core re-vendored, and I3 hashes the judge parameters.

cards.title: Hop 0 crowded out the graph
cards.failed: Rule 7 sorts by hop first, so a seed's own passages fill every slot.
cards.cost: With no deeper passage, the relation labels cannot change H's list. Under the projection, gate 3 would trigger and H2 would be lost.
cards.fix: Addendum D: a per-hop quota (4/3/3 at 10), backfill in rule-7 order, the same output order; an equal cap, not an equal length.

cards.title: Deeper hops needed scores
cards.failed: The quota ranks inside every hop, so every passage at hops 0 to 2 needs a cross-encoder score.
cards.cost: 181,630 new pairs, on machines that could score differently.
cards.fix: One scorer source by a rule fixed in advance: 25/25 kernels matched 200 old scores exactly, so S1 was kept and the merged file was hashed before tuning.
